title: Grad: Intelligent Microservice Scaling by Harnessing Resource Fungibility
problem: Microservice applications deployed alongside co-located services suffer resource contention that degrades end-to-end latency; existing auto-scaling solutions focus only on scaling critical (bottleneck) microservices and ignore non-critical microservices, missing resource efficiency opportunities through inter-service resource fungibility.
motivation: Cloud operators need to maximize resource utilization while maintaining SLA compliance; exploiting resource fungibility between critical and non-critical microservices can simultaneously reduce resource waste and prevent latency violations.
method: Grad uses three components: (1) a modular learning approach that profiles individual microservice latency as a function of environmental conditions (resource allocation, interference); (2) gradient-based extraction from these profiles to design a scalable optimization module that dynamically selects the optimal set of microservices to scale (both critical and non-critical); (3) an end-to-end latency predictor serving as a real-time simulator to provide rapid feedback during SLA violation response. Evaluated on real microservice benchmarks and production traces.
key_novelty: Gradient-based resource fungibility framework that jointly optimizes scaling of both critical and non-critical microservices by modeling their latency-resource trade-offs and inter-service resource substitutability.
contributions: Identification that non-critical microservice scaling via resource fungibility can improve efficiency alongside critical microservice scaling.
Modular learning approach profiling individual microservice latency vs. resource/environment conditions with gradient extraction.
Scalable gradient-based optimization module for dynamic joint microservice selection for scaling.
49.1% resource usage reduction and 3.7x fewer SLA violations vs. state-of-the-art on real production traces.

metrics.other: 49.1% resource usage reduction; 3.7x lower SLA violation probability vs. state-of-the-art

limitations: The gradient-based profiling approach requires representative training traces; effectiveness in highly dynamic or unpredictable production environments with frequent workload shifts may degrade.
primary_theme: Gradient-based joint microservice scaling exploiting resource fungibility
